body.p: This paper responds to the Examiner's Non-Final Office Action mailed on
October 23, 2024. Reconsideration and continued examination in view of the foregoing response is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-20 are currently pending in the instant application, with claims 1, 12, and 18 being independent. By the present document, the Applicants present amendments to claims 1, 12 and 17-18 which respectfully are believed to overcome the rejections to the recent Office action dated October 23, 2024. Support for the amendments is found in the original claims as filed. No new matter has been added. By the present document, Applicants have canceled dependent claims 2, 16, and 20.

The Office Action objects to the specification based on informalities related to paragraphs [0017] and [0018]. Applicants thank the Examiner for pointing out these informalities and submits along with the present response an amendment to the specification to correct the same informalities. No new matter is raised by the amendments to the specification. Accordingly, Applicants respectfully request the withdrawal of the objections.

The Office Action rejects claims 1, 4, 6, 8-14, 16-18, and 20 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over the article entitled Object-Based Activity Recognition With Heterogeneous Sensors On Wrist by Maekawa et al. ("Maekawa") in view of the article entitled Measuring Physical Activity of Older Adults Via Smartwatch and Stigmergic Receptive Fields by Alfeo et al. ("Alfeo"). Applicants respectfully traverse these rejections.
In rejecting independent claims 1, 12, and 18 the Office Action cites to Alfeo as disclosing the claimed "inflection points" of the present application. However, a closer

reading of Alfeo reveals that the definition of inflection points, as used in the reference, is entirely different from how it is used in the present application. The claims as amended recite "extracts inflection points from the multimodal dataset.... the inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand." Alfeo simply refers to "a multi-sigmoidal function, characterized by a couple of inflection points, for each region of interest," and therefore fails to recite inflections points that "[correspond] to the movement of the hand and fingers of the hand." In Alfeo, the "inflection points" disclosed are merely the minimum and maximum data points of a multi-sigmoidal function, and there is no indication anywhere within the reference that those minimum and maximum data points of the function correspond to the movement of the hand and fingers of the hand. Nor does Alfeo disclose "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." In fact, Alfeo only recites the term "inflection points" a total of four times, all in reference to the same definition of a minimum or maximum data point on a sigmoidal function, and all without any indication that they "correspond to the movement of the hands and fingers of the hand" or "the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." Alfeo, pg 3.
Although the office action states that the claim language "corresponding to

movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" is disclosed by Maekawa, the Applicants respectfully submit that this is irrelevant as the claim language is directed specifically to "inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" not just "corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand." Office Action pg, 4. The claim limitation as written cannot be separated into two distinct elements that are attributable to separate references. Even if Maekawa allegedly discloses "movement of the hand and fingers of the hand," the reference completely fails to disclose inflection points that correspond to such hand and finger movement. The same arguments may be said regarding the citation to Maekawa as disclosing "corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest" from the claim element "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task." In order to remedy this deficiency, the Office Action cites to Alfeo as disclosing the "inflection points," but as explained above, the use of the term "inflection points" in Alfeo provides

a completely different definition from how it is used in the present application. Therefore, neither Maekawa nor Alfeo teach, suggest, or disclose every limitation of the independent claims because they fail to teach the claimed "inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand."

In sum, Maekawa in combination with Alfeo fails to teach or suggest each and every element of the independent claims and a person having ordinary skill in the art would not be motivated to combine the cited references to arrive at the claimed invention because there is no indication in Alfeo that the "inflection points" are anything beyond minimum and maximum data points from a sigmoidal function. Applicants therefore respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of independent claims 1, 12, and 18, followed by an indication of allowance thereof. Dependent claims 4, 6, 8- 11, 13-14, 16-17, and 20 depend from, directly or indirectly, and necessarily incorporate each and every element of independent claims 1, 12 and 18. Applicants therefore also respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of claims 4, 6, 8-11, 13-14, 16- 17, and 20, followed by an indication of allowance thereof.

The Office Action rejects claim 2 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Maekawa in view of Alfeo, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2020/0005615 to Madden et al. ("Madden"). Applicants respectfully traverse these rejections.
As outlined above, Maekawa as combined with Alfeo fails to teach or suggest

each and every limitation of independent claim 1 because they fail to teach the inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" and "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." Madden in combination with Maekawa and Alfeo fails to cure this deficiency. Claim 2 directly depends from, and necessarily incorporates every limitation of independent claim 1. Applicants therefore respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of claim 2, followed by an indication of allowance thereof.

The Office Action rejects claims 3 and 15 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Maekawa in view of Alfeo, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2011/0182469 to Ji et al. ("Ji"). Applicants respectfully traverse these rejections.
As outlined above, Maekawa as combined with Alfeo fails to teach or suggest

each and every limitation of independent claims 1 and 12 because they fail to teach the inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" and "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." Ji in combination with Maekawa and Alfeo fails to cure this deficiency. Claims 3 and 15 directly depend from, and necessarily incorporate every limitation of independent claims 1 and 12. Applicants therefore respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of claims 3 and 15, followed by an indication of allowance thereof.

The Office Action rejects claims 5 and 19 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Maekawa in view of Alfeo, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0218474 to Yamazaki et al. ("Yamazaki"). Applicants respectfully traverse these rejections.
As outlined above, Maekawa as combined with Alfeo fails to teach or suggest

each and every limitation of independent claims 1 and 18 because they fail to teach the inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" and "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." Yamazaki in combination with Maekawa and Alfeo fails to cure this deficiency. Claims 5 and 19 directly depend from, and necessarily incorporate every limitation of independent claims 1 and 18. Applicants therefore respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of claims 5 and 19, followed by an indication of allowance thereof.

The Office Action rejects claim 7 under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Maekawa in view of Alfeo, and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2008/0274819 to Caldwell et al. ("Caldwell"). Applicants respectfully traverse these rejections.
As outlined above, Maekawa as combined with Alfeo fails to teach or suggest

each and every limitation of independent claim 1 because they fail to teach the inflection points corresponding to movement of the hand and fingers of the hand" and "at least one of the inflection points corresponding to the predetermined task associated with the object of interest." Caldwell in combination with Maekawa and Alfeo fails to cure this deficiency. Claim 7 directly depends from, and necessarily incorporates every limitation of independent claim 1. Applicants therefore respectfully request the withdrawal of the §103 rejection of claim 7, followed by an indication of allowance thereof.

By the present response, the Applicants respectfully submit that the claims are in condition for allowance, and notification to that effect is earnestly requested.
